cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the saints in Ephesus (Ephesians 1:1). He just told them they've been saved by grace through faith, the gift of God, not by works (Ephesians 2:8-9). Now he turns to the Gentiles and says, "Therefore remember."

cards.question: Paul says the people known as the so-called circumcision had a name for the Gentiles. What was it?

cards.text: Then Paul tells them to remember what life was like at that time. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, NOBODY loves that trip down memory lane.

cards.question: Back then, Paul says, the Gentiles were separate from ___ and alienated from the commonwealth of ___.
Paul's list of how things used to be keeps going. What else does he say the Gentiles were strangers to?
Paul says that back then, the Gentiles were without hope and without God in the world.

cards.text: Then Paul hits the turn: "But now," and friend, that's the sound of a drawer sliding open. In Christ Jesus, the Gentiles who were once far away have been brought near.

cards.question: Paul says the Gentiles who were far away have been brought near through the ___ of Christ.

cards.text: So how did the far-away ones get brought near? Paul says Christ Himself is our peace.

cards.question: Paul says Christ made the Gentiles and Israel one by tearing down a wall between them.

cards.text: That dividing wall of hostility? GONE, and no orange cones blocking traffic for six months either. Christ did it by abolishing in His flesh the law of commandments and decrees.

cards.question: Christ did all this to create something in Himself out of the two, making peace. What did He create?
Paul says Christ reconciled both the Gentiles and Israel to God in one body through the ___.

cards.text: And Christ didn't just make peace, friend. He came and preached it.

cards.question: Christ came and preached peace. Who did He preach it to?

answers.text: those far away and those near
only those who were far away

cards.question: Paul says that through Christ, only the ones who were near have access to the Father.

cards.text: So Paul says the Gentiles are no longer strangers and foreigners. No more standing by the door at a party where you don't know a soul, holding one cookie and pretending to check your phone.

cards.question: Paul says the Gentiles are now fellow ___ with the saints and members of God's ___.

cards.text: Then Paul switches pictures: God's household is a building, built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets. And as a guy who goes EVERYWHERE on a gold base, let me tell you, I respect a good foundation.

cards.question: In the building Paul describes, who is the cornerstone?
In Christ, Paul says, the whole building is fitted together and grows into a holy ___ in the Lord.
Paul tells the Gentiles in Ephesus that they aren't part of this building.

cards.text: Paul says they too are being built together into a dwelling place for God in His Spirit. I went from a junk drawer to a bakery and thought THAT was a glow-up, friend, but this one beats my story by a mile.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 11 mentions orange, a food that isn't a cookie and isn't in the passage.

rule.text: In jokes and comparisons, cookies are the only food he mentions.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to supply the exact wording of the next item in Paul's list in 2:12, 'the covenants of the promise.' No earlier card points toward covenants or promises, so the baker can only guess the wording. It doesn't test movement or meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The statement says Christ made the two one 'by tearing down a wall.' Ephesians 2:14 joins the two with 'and' ('has made the two one and has torn down the dividing wall of hostility'). It never says the first happened by means of the second, so the card adds a 'how' connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Ephesians 2:18 appears only as a false true-or-false statement ('only the ones who were near have access'). No card ever says what the verse actually says: that through Christ both groups have access to the Father by one Spirit. The baker leaves without that detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card uses 'God's household' from Ephesians 2:19 but cites only Ephesians 2:20. The citation should run from the first verse the card uses to the last.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
